rationale: The printed entry’s human-eye core is the best explanation of the exact texts it groups: Matthew 6:22-23 read with Proverbs 22:9 and 23:6 (and the mammon/treasure context) makes the lamp’s light track a bountiful/giving eye versus an evil/withholding eye more tightly than a freestanding ‘spiritual perception’ label. That core is therefore carried by the cited witnesses. The further printed claim that God’s fiery eyes are His righteous watchers who shine like the stars is a chapter-driven identification that over-links Zechariah 4:10, Revelation 1:14, and Revelation 5:6; those verses are explained more directly by divine omniscience/the seven Spirits without equating the eyes themselves with the saints. Hence PERSUADED on the adjudicated core, CORE_ONLY because that secondary assertion in the entry is not supported.
book_core_identification: The eye is the lamp of the body that reveals the light within, such that a good eye gives and an evil eye withholds.
book_secondary_elaborations: God's fiery eyes are His righteous watchers
Those watchers range throughout the earth
Those watchers shine like the stars in heaven
unsupported_glossary_assertions: God's fiery eyes are His righteous watchers who shine like the stars in heaven
chapter_only_objections: The chapter’s full equation of the eye-studded living creatures, Christ’s flaming eyes, the eyes of the LORD, the seven Spirits, and the righteous-as-stars into one referent class goes beyond what the glossary sentence itself must assert and is not required by the plain wording of Rev 5:6.
Sun=Father / moon=Son / stars=court-and-tribes / Mazzaroth-gate typology is chapter scaffolding, not a claim printed in the Eye entry.
Use of the Hebrew Revelation and planetary/satyr side-arguments is chapter-only apparatus.
strongest_counter_interpretation: In Scripture the eye most commonly figures spiritual perception and the inner moral condition (the eye as lamp filling the body with light or darkness); the good/evil-eye idiom can mean generosity versus stinginess in specific proverbial and Matthean contexts; references to the eyes of the LORD, eyes as a flame of fire, and the Lamb’s seven eyes denote divine omniscience, judgment, and the seven Spirits of God sent into the earth—not human righteous ones identified with the stars.
counter_core_identification: Eye = spiritual perception / inner moral light; God’s (and the Lamb’s) eyes = divine omniscience, watchfulness, and the Spirit(s).
material_core_denial: The counter does not deny that the eye is a lamp revealing inner light or that good/evil eye language tracks giving versus withholding; it only rejects equating God’s fiery eyes with the righteous as star-like watchers.
counter_case: Matthew 6:22-23 and Luke 11:34-36 are widely and naturally read as the inner person’s enlightenment or darkness, matching Ephesians 1:18, Psalm 119:18, and the blindness/sight motif elsewhere.
Revelation 5:6 explicitly identifies the seven eyes as the seven Spirits of God, not as the saints.
Zechariah 4:10 and parallel ‘eyes of the LORD’ texts (e.g., 2 Chronicles 16:9; Proverbs 15:3) read straightforwardly as God’s own ranging knowledge and care.
Revelation 1:14’s fiery eyes fit the stock theophany of penetrating divine judgment without requiring the eyes to be people.
Daniel 12:3 (righteous shine as stars) is a separate simile and does not turn stars into the referent of ‘God’s eyes.’
book_explanatory_advantages: Unifies the lamp saying with the concrete Hebrew idiom tov ayin / ra ayin (Proverbs 22:9; 23:6) instead of leaving two disconnected senses.
Fits Matthew 6:22-23 inside its immediate treasure/mammon unit (6:19-24) and the ‘evil eye’ of Matthew 20:15.
Gives a single mechanical picture: the eye-lamp burns by what it gives, so generosity fills the body with light and withholding with darkness.
counter_explanatory_advantages: Preserves the explicit apposition in Revelation 5:6 (eyes = seven Spirits).
Keeps ‘eyes of the LORD’ as divine attribute rather than human agents, matching the dominant OT usage.
Avoids a multi-step chain (beasts’ eyes → LORD’s eyes → Spirits → flaming eyes of Christ → stars → righteous) that the glossary entry compresses into one claim.
Accounts for the broad NT blindness/sight and ‘eyes of the heart’ corpus without forcing every eye text through the generosity idiom.
unresolved_objections: Whether ‘revealing the light within’ is fully exhausted by giving/withholding or still needs a residual ‘single/healthy perception’ sense remains debatable even after the Proverbs link.
The entry’s terse apposition ‘God’s fiery eyes — His righteous watchers’ is not entailed by the six listed references alone without the chapter’s longer star-court argument.
